content.value_statement: Technical debt slows delivery, raises defect rates, and makes planning difficult. This skill turns debt signals into measured remediation plans with ROI.
actual_capabilities: Inventories code, architecture, testing, documentation, and infrastructure debt categories.
Estimates velocity, quality, and risk impact for each debt item.
Creates debt dashboards with complexity, duplication, coverage, and dependency health metrics.
Prioritizes remediation into quick wins, medium-term work, and long-term initiatives.
Defines prevention gates for commits, CI, reviews, and debt budgets.
Produces stakeholder summaries, developer guidance, and ROI projections.
limitations: Results depend on access to the relevant repository, history, tests, and dependency data.
Cost and ROI estimates need validation against local salaries, defect rates, and delivery metrics.
The skill plans refactoring work but does not automatically change code.
It cannot replace security, performance, or architecture reviews by domain owners.

use_cases.title: Plan a Refactoring Sprint
use_cases.description: Identify high-value debt items and convert them into scoped work for the next sprint.

use_cases.title: Assess Legacy Code Risk
use_cases.description: Map risky modules, missing tests, and dependency problems before changing a legacy system.

use_cases.title: Build an Executive Debt Report
use_cases.description: Summarize debt cost, delivery impact, and expected return for stakeholders.

prompt_templates.title: Find Basic Debt Hotspots
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this repository for duplicated code, long files, complex functions, weak tests, and missing documentation. Give me the top five debt hotspots.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Remediation Backlog
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the debt in this codebase and create a prioritized backlog. Include effort, expected benefit, risk, owners, and acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Quantify Debt Cost
prompt_templates.prompt: Estimate the monthly cost of the main technical debt items. Use defect rates, change frequency, duplicated work, and test gaps where evidence exists.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Debt Reduction Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a quarterly technical debt reduction strategy. Include metrics, roadmap, staffing model, quality gates, communication plan, and ROI assumptions.

output_examples.input: A team asks why feature work keeps slowing down in a legacy service.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a ranked debt inventory, identifies the highest-cost modules, estimates monthly velocity loss, and recommends quick wins for the next sprint.

output_examples.input: A tech lead needs a plan before splitting a large service.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines coupling risks, missing tests, migration phases, quality gates, and stakeholder checkpoints for the refactoring effort.

output_examples.input: An engineering manager needs budget support for debt work.
output_examples.output: The skill produces an executive summary with cost drivers, risk levels, projected savings, and a quarter-by-quarter remediation roadmap.

best_practices: Provide repository context, test results, dependency data, and recent defect patterns before asking for cost estimates.
Ask for debt items to be ranked by impact, effort, risk, and confidence.
Validate recommendations with code owners before scheduling major refactors.
anti_patterns: Do not treat every style issue as technical debt with business impact.
Do not start large refactors without tests, rollback plans, and stakeholder alignment.
Do not use synthetic ROI numbers without documenting assumptions and confidence.

faq.question: Does this skill edit code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It analyzes technical debt and creates remediation plans. Code changes require a separate implementation workflow.

faq.question: Can it analyze architecture debt?
faq.answer: Yes. It looks for boundary violations, missing abstractions, coupling, monolithic components, and modernization needs.

faq.question: What inputs improve the analysis?
faq.answer: Repository files, test coverage, dependency reports, incident history, defect data, and delivery metrics improve the output.

faq.question: How does it prioritize debt?
faq.answer: It compares impact, effort, risk, confidence, and expected return, then separates quick wins from larger initiatives.

faq.question: Can it help prevent new debt?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends quality gates for commits, CI, code review, coverage, dependencies, and architecture checks.

faq.question: Is it suitable for executive reporting?
faq.answer: Yes. It can produce concise summaries with cost estimates, risk levels, investment needs, and ROI projections.
